correctness.summary: The Fourier multiplier gives an exact one-dimensional defect identity for arbitrary transverse cutoffs. Dominated convergence yields the H^{1/2} law. For interval unions, the endpoint Fourier expansion reduces the problem to one universal cosine integral; its Mellin transform gives the constant 5/2-log 2, and the interval specialization agrees with direct numerical evaluation.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: The direct source arXiv:2609.15155 proves only an upper O(sqrt(epsilon |log epsilon|)) relative rate for its truncated strip and later uses that cost as a model for quantitative stability. Repository and external searches did not locate the matching constant, second term, arbitrary-cutoff identity, or finite-perimeter extension. Relevant older double-Hilbert papers concern different singular-integral operators or dyadic commutators. The main residual risk is an unindexed contemporaneous refinement because the source is very recent.

value.summary: The result makes the source model computation sharp, identifies the hard-cutoff logarithm as an H^{1/2} endpoint effect, and shows that the leading finite-perimeter coefficient is universal while the next term records logarithmic interactions among boundary points.

limitations: Only diagonal tubes with transverse cutoffs are analyzed; no general near-invariant-set classification is proved.
The finite-perimeter expansion fixes the one-dimensional set as epsilon tends to zero and is not uniform under endpoint collisions.
No global extremality statement among bounded planar sets is claimed.
The quantitative-stability question in arXiv:2609.15155 remains open.
A contemporaneous unindexed overlap may exist because the direct source is very recent.
Independent audit has not been performed.
